notes:
I couldn't write these notes, because I didn't manage to read any sources. On my first attempt I tried to open eight pages at once (Enduring Word, Bible Hub's commentary page, Gill and Ellicott on Bible Hub, Precept Austin, the NET Bible notes, Augustine on New Advent and the Treasury of Scripture Knowledge on StudyLight). That went over the tool's usage limit, and none of the pages loaded. When I retried with just Enduring Word, the tool told me I had no calls left for this turn.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say and to leave out what I couldn't find. Since I found nothing, I have no notes to give you. I haven't filled the gap from memory, because those notes wouldn't have URLs behind them.

If you ask again in a new message, I'll open the pages a few at a time and write the notes verse by verse with a URL for each point. I'd start with these:
- **Traditional reading:** enduringword.com/bible-commentary/psalm-62/, then Gill, Ellicott and the Pulpit Commentary on biblehub.com, then preceptaustin.org.
- **Modern scholarship:** the NET Bible notes on Psalm 62 at netbible.org.
- **Catholic and Orthodox:** Augustine's exposition on newadvent.org. His Bible numbers the Psalms differently, so our Psalm 62 is his Psalm 61.
- **Differences between Protestant traditions:** searches on the Reformed, Baptist, Methodist, Pentecostal and Lutheran sites. I'd look especially at "God alone" (vv. 1–2, 5–6), the wealth warning (v. 10), and "repay each man according to his deeds" (v. 12), which may bear on how faith and works are taught.
- **Prosperity teaching:** only if the allowed sites discuss Psalm 62 in that light.
